en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 16.13.
Kusala-ttika, Āsava-gocchaka.
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome and an outflow (*āsava*),

there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor an outflow … [and so on] … a state that is neither wholesome nor an outflow … [and so on] … a state that is neither indeterminate nor an outflow … [and so on] … states that are neither wholesome nor an outflow and neither indeterminate nor an outflow … [and so on] … states that are neither wholesome nor an outflow and unwholesome and an outflow arise by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). Under the root condition:
Five [ways], with respect to the object, three … pe … five [ways] with respect to non-disappearance.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not associated with the taints (anāsava), a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with the taints arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not associated with the taints, a state that is neither indeterminate nor associated with the taints … pe … a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with the taints [arises].

And neither-indeterminate-nor-outflow-dharmas arise by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). [Under] the root [condition], there are three; ... pe ... [under] the non-disappearance [condition], there are three.
Dependent on an indeterminate dharma associated with outflows (*sāsava*) ... pe ... (Similar to the mundane dyad.
Dependent on an unwholesome dharma associated with outflows, an unwholesome dharma not associated with outflows arises ... pe ...

A state that is neither wholesome nor associated with taints … pe … a state that is neither indeterminate nor associated with taints … pe … states that are neither wholesome nor associated with taints and neither indeterminate nor associated with taints … pe … states that are neither wholesome nor associated with taints and neither unwholesome nor associated with taints arise by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
In the case of the root condition there are five; in the case of the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) … [and so forth].
Three ... [and so on] ... five in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on an unwholesome state dissociated from the taints, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor dissociated from the taints ... [and so on] ...

a state that is neither indeterminate nor dissociated from the taints ... [and so on] ... a state that is neither wholesome nor dissociated from the taints and neither indeterminate nor dissociated from the taints.

States that are dissociated from the taints (*āsava*) arise with root-cause condition (*hetu-paccaya*). Under the root-cause condition there are three; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition there are three.
Dependent on unwholesome states that are both taints and associated with taints (*āsava*), there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor dissociated from taints ...
pe ... a state that is neither wholesome nor dissociated from taints ... pe ... a state that is neither indeterminate nor dissociated from taints ... pe ... [and so forth].

A phenomenon that is neither with-outflows (*sāsrava*) nor without-outflows (*anāsrava*) ... [and so on] ... phenomena that are neither wholesome (*kuśala*), nor with-outflows, nor without-outflows, nor indeterminate (*avyākṛta*), nor with-outflows, nor without-outflows ...

[and so on] ... phenomena that are neither wholesome, nor with-outflows, nor without-outflows, nor unwholesome, nor with-outflows, nor without-outflows arise by way of the root-condition (*hetu-pratyaya*).
In the case of the root-condition there are five; in the case of the object-condition (*ālambana*) there are three ... [and so on] ... in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*) there are five.
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome, associated with the taints (*sāsava*), and not itself a taint (*anāsava*), there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor a taint,

and is also not itself a taint … [and so on] … dependent on a state that is neither indeterminate (*abyākata*) nor a taint, and is also not itself a taint … [and so on] … dependent on states that are neither wholesome nor a taint,
and are also not themselves taints, and are neither indeterminate nor a taint, and are also not themselves taints, [other such] states arise by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
In the case of the root condition (*hetu*), there are three; ... [and so on] ... in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*), there are three.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both an outflow (*āsava*) and associated with outflows, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor an outflow and is not dissociated from outflows; ... [and so on] ...
a state that is neither indeterminate nor an outflow and is not dissociated from outflows; ... [and so on] ... a state that is neither wholesome...

States that are neither cankers (*āsava*) nor dissociated from cankers, which are neither indeterminate nor cankers, and which are neither cankers nor dissociated from cankers, arise with root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
[Under] root [condition], there are three; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance condition, there are three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is associated with cankers but is not itself a canker, [arises] a state that is neither wholesome nor dissociated from cankers...
A state that is neither-outflow nor an outflow ... [etc. ... a state that is neither-indeterminate-nor-dissociated-from-outflows, neither-outflow nor an outflow ...

[etc. ... states that are neither-wholesome-nor-dissociated-from-outflows, neither-outflow-nor-an-outflow, and neither-indeterminate-nor-dissociated-from-outflows, as well as states that are outflows, arise by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
There are three [answers] under the root-condition ... [etc. ... there are three [answers] under the non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*).
Dependent on an indeterminate state that is dissociated from the taints but is subject to the taints … [and so on] … (It is similar to the "Worldly" dyad.)
